nc_white_monster_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder in the North End boulderfield below Moore's Wall at Hanging Rock State Park. Its eleven problems start around V2 and climb through the middle grades to a cluster of hard lines in the V8 to V10 range, so it suits strong boulderers more than beginners. The style is steep and tension-heavy, with open-handed slopers, pinches and the odd slot jug, and heel-toe skills pay off. The face sees no direct sun and can stay damp after rain, with the air cooling off by early afternoon. Most lines are tall enough to want several pads and a few spotters, so bring a group.

nc_10_the_fortress.blurb: A popular spine of quartzite on the summit ridge of Crowders Mountain, in the main climbing section of the state park near Kings Mountain. Ten routes, nearly all of them traditional with a single top-rope line, run from easy fifth class up to the low 5.10s, with most clustered right around 5.10. The rock is solid and a cave with steep overhanging lines makes the wall easy to recognise. Fixed anchors on top make top-roping straightforward, and the wall is often crowded on nice weekends. It is a short walk along the ridge from the Practice Wall, so it suits a quick day with a standard trad rack.

nc_11_middle_finger_wall.blurb: The west face of a north-south rock ridge at Crowders Mountain State Park, part of the main climbing section. About ten routes here are mostly traditional, with a few top-rope options, spanning from easy fifth class through the 5.7 range up to a single route near 5.9. The easiest lines are two-pitch outings that suit newer leaders, while others ask for a standard trad rack and a gear anchor at the top. Some of the upper rock is sharp and has loose holds, so wear a helmet. The wall is reached by dropping down a small trail from the summit path.

nc_cave_the_2.blurb: A dark, shaded cave on the south face of Rumbling Bald near Chimney Rock, reached by moving right and down from the Screamweaver area. Ten routes mix trad and sport: several moderate lines from 5.7 to 5.9+ that can also be top-roped, one trad line in the 5.11 range, and a handful of steeper sport pitches climbing into the 5.12s. Because the cave stays in shade it tends to be most pleasant on warm days, and the rock is the gneiss typical of the crag. It makes a good change of pace from the sunnier walls nearby.

nc_stu_s_boulder.blurb: One large, isolated boulder in the Central Area boulderfield beneath Sentinel Buttress on Moore's Wall at Hanging Rock State Park. Its ten problems run from an easy warm-up through a solid block of mid-grade lines, mostly V4 to V5, up to a couple of harder problems in the V6 to V8 range, making it a good stop for climbers across the spectrum. Several lines are well-liked, including a friction-heavy test piece and a blocky arete. To find it, go through the main boulder field past the first large boulders, then continue under an overhanging face until it comes into view.

nc_underworld_the.blurb: A steep cave-like crag on the west side of Linville Gorge, in the Gold Coast Cliffs just below Sunshine Point. Ten routes are mostly bolted sport lines, with a couple of trad pitches and one aid project. Grades start with an easy crack and one 5.10 sport line, then stack up at 5.11 and especially 5.12, with a 5.13 project, so this is a destination for strong sport climbers. The overhanging walls are known as some of the steepest sport climbing in the High Country. Getting down involves a rappel or a fixed-line descent, followed by muddy slab scrambling to the base.
